summary: A round-eight AFLW roundup led by Richmond's 11-point comeback win over Hawthorn in Cairns, which kept their finals hopes alive. It also covers West Coast beating Essendon, Collingwood holding off Geelong, Fremantle beating St Kilda, Sydney thrashing the Western Bulldogs, Narrm beating North Melbourne, and Brisbane edging Adelaide. Other items include Richelle Cranston's kidney disease disclosure and Najwa Allen's record ban.
one_line: AFLW round eight roundup: Richmond come back to beat Hawthorn in Cairns, plus results from Essendon, Geelong, St Kilda, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane games.
key_facts: Richmond beat Hawthorn 6.5 (41) to 4.6 (30) at Cazaly's Stadium in Cairns on Friday night, their first win in four games.

Richmond trailed by nine points entering the last quarter, and Hawthorn scored just one point in the final term; Emelia Yassir kicked a late goal on her third attempt and Caitlin Greiser sealed it with a 45-metre goal.
Monique Conti had 35 disposals and seven clearances for Richmond; Katie Brennan kicked two goals in her 50th game.
West Coast beat Essendon 3.5 (23) to 2.7 (19) at Windy Hill for their second win of the season, a week after coach Michael Prior's comments following a 70-point loss to Melbourne.
Collingwood beat Geelong by six points at Victoria Park in wind and rain; ruck Sabrina Frederick had 39 hit-outs.
Fremantle beat St Kilda 6.9 (45) to 3.3 (21) at Fremantle Oval, scoring 26 points in the first quarter, their highest-scoring quarter of the season, and dashing the Saints' finals hopes.
Western Bulldogs forward Richelle Cranston, 34, revealed she is playing with stage five chronic kidney disease.
Sydney beat the Western Bulldogs 14.12 (96) to 6.3 (39), the Dogs' eighth straight loss and biggest defeat; Chloe Molloy kicked 3.4 from 28 possessions.
Narrm (Melbourne) beat North Melbourne 5.7 (37) to 2.2 (14) at Ikon Park to reclaim top spot on the ladder.
Brisbane Lions beat Adelaide 5.12 (42) to 6.3 (39) at Brighton Homes Arena, ending Adelaide's unbeaten run; Lily Postlethwaite's behind broke the stalemate.
Adelaide's Najwa Allen received a three-match ban, the longest in AFLW history, for a high bump on Kirsten McLeod of the Western Bulldogs.
Greater Western Sydney beat Carlton by two points, 8.1 (49) to 7.5 (47), denying Carlton a chance to move into the top eight.
